subject: Astronomy & Space
title: The Chicxulub Impact
description: A fast breakdown of The Chicxulub Impact for builders.

hook.text: 66 million years ago, a 10 km asteroid hit Mexico. It ended the age of dinosaurs in hours.

buildup.text: The impact released energy equal to 10 billion nuclear bombs. A fireball spread across a thousand km.

discovery.text: The crater was found under Mexico's Yucatán in 1978—180 km wide and buried for millions of years.

twist.text: Dinosaurs had thrived for 165 million years. One bad day erased 75% of all species on Earth.

climax.text: The impact cleared the way for mammals. Without that asteroid, humans might never have evolved.

punchline.text: One rock, one bad day. Dinosaurs out, mammals in.

quiz.question: What percentage of species went extinct after the Chicxulub impact?

details.summary: About 66 million years ago, a 10-kilometer asteroid struck present-day Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula, creating the 180-kilometer Chicxulub crater. The impact ejected enough dust and debris to block sunlight globally, triggering mass extinction that killed 75% of all species — including the non-avian…
details.whyItMatters: The Chicxulub impact proves that asteroids can cause global catastrophe and mass extinction. It ended the age of dinosaurs and enabled mammals — and eventually humans — to rise. It's the definitive case for why planetary defense matters.
takeaways: A 10 km asteroid struck Earth 66 million years ago in Mexico
It caused a mass extinction killing 75% of species including dinosaurs
The 180 km crater was discovered in the late 1970s

faq.question: How do we know an asteroid killed the dinosaurs?
faq.answer: A worldwide layer of iridium-rich clay marks the exact extinction boundary. Iridium is rare on Earth but common in asteroids. Discovery of the buried Chicxulub crater, shocked quartz, impact glass, and tsunami deposits all confirm a massive impact at exactly the right time — 66 million years ago.

faq.question: What happened in the hours and years after impact?
faq.answer: Within hours: a thermal pulse ignited wildfires globally and a mega-tsunami swept coastlines. Within weeks: dust and soot blocked sunlight, dropping temperatures by 15-25°C. Photosynthesis collapsed, food chains broke, and acid rain polluted waters. Recovery took hundreds of thousands of years.
